title: Scotch Eggs
subtitle: Soft-boiled eggs wrapped in sausagemeat and fried
excerpt: A soft-boiled egg encased in seasoned sausagemeat, coated in breadcrumbs, and deep-fried until golden. The yolk should be just set and slightly runny when you cut one open.

recipe.sourceNotes: Scotch eggs are a British picnic and pub food that has been sold at Fortnum and Mason since at least 1738. The classic version wraps a hard-boiled egg in sausagemeat, coats it in breadcrumbs, and deep-fries the whole thing. The modern preference is for a soft-boiled egg with a still-runny yolk, which requires precise timing: 6 minutes in boiling water gives a yolk that is just set on the outside but still molten in the centre after the second cooking in the fryer. The sausagemeat can be seasoned simply or given additions of mustard, herbs, or chilli. Scotch eggs are eaten warm or cold, at picnics, at the pub, and in sandwiches.

recipeTools.notes: For frying; a deep, heavy-based saucepan.

content.text: The eggs need two separate cookings: the initial soft boil and the frying. Get a bowl of iced water ready before you start: plunging the eggs straight from the boiling water into ice water stops the cooking immediately and makes them easier to peel. The sausagemeat must be wrapped thinly and evenly around each egg, with no gaps or thick patches, or it will cook unevenly. Chill the assembled eggs before frying to help the coating hold together.
Cook 4 eggs in boiling water for exactly 6 minutes. Transfer immediately to iced water. Once cold, peel carefully.
Mix the sausagemeat with the mustard, thyme, salt, and pepper. Divide into 4 equal portions. On a piece of cling film, flatten each portion into a thin oval, large enough to wrap a whole egg.
Roll each peeled egg in flour. Wrap tightly in sausagemeat, pressing the joins firmly to seal. Dip in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs to coat all over. Chill for 30 minutes.

Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pan to 170 C. Fry the eggs in batches for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper. Rest for 2 minutes before cutting in half to serve.
